notes: Kitchen sinks and bathroom sinks scored within one framework. Sub-type (kitchen_stainless, kitchen_fireclay, kitchen_cast_iron, kitchen_composite, bathroom_vitreous_china, bathroom_fireclay) is a key differentiator but does NOT create an automatic tier advantage — a premium stainless kitchen sink and a premium fireclay farmhouse sink can both be Tier 1. For stainless: gauge, steel grade (T-304/T-316), construction method, and sound deadening are THE critical specs. For fireclay/cast iron: body density, glaze quality, and manufacturing origin. For composite: stone-to-resin ratio and heat resistance. For bathroom: china quality, glazing, and rim engineering. Kohler appeared 187 times in luxury home listings. Shares methodology with faucets — material quality and construction method drive the score, not aesthetics. Performance axis is essentially flat (all sinks drain water at regulated rates).

products.name: Rohl Shaws Original Lancaster Fireclay Farmhouse (RC3618)

tier_anchors.notes: Rohl Shaws: handcrafted English fireclay, kiln-fired in Darwen Lancashire at 2100°F+, each sink individually crafted with slight variations — artisanal quality signal. Sold through Rohl (Fortune Brands Innovations). Fireclay is non-porous, chip-resistant, stain-resistant. No mass production — genuine heirloom construction. Professional consensus places Shaws at or near top for fireclay. Kohler Whitehaven: self-trimming apron-front cast iron with porcelain enamel glaze — Kohler's proprietary enamel process is industry benchmark. Cast iron body = massive thermal mass, vibration-free, zero sound concerns. Kohler WI manufacturing heritage. 187 Kohler sightings in luxury listings confirms brand positioning.

products.name: Blanco IKON 33 Silgranit Composite Apron Front (401734)

tier_anchors.notes: Blanco IKON: 80% granite composite (Silgranit patented formula), heat-rated to 536°F (280°C), scratch/stain/impact-resistant. German-engineered (Oberderdingen HQ). First composite apron-front sink. Blanco holds 35+ patents on Silgranit material. Professional consensus: near-indestructible, low maintenance, hides marks well. Kohler Cairn: Neoroc composite (proprietary), matte finish, undermount. Kohler engineering applied to composite. Slightly below Blanco on composite material heritage but Kohler backing and ecosystem.

Kraus Standart PRO: 16-gauge T-304 stainless, NoiseDefend sound deadening (80% coverage), TRU16 real 16-gauge certification, commercial-grade satin finish. Best value-to-quality ratio in stainless. Professional plumber consensus: reliable, thick, well-engineered drain slope. Kohler Caxton: vitreous china undermount bathroom sink — Kohler's most popular bathroom undermount. Clean lines, consistent glaze quality. Standard vitreous china construction. Massive aftermarket and parts availability. The bathroom sink benchmark.

Glacier Bay: Home Depot house brand. 22-gauge stainless (thin). Minimal sound deadening. Drop-in installation (least premium mounting). Unknown OEM manufacturing. T-304 claimed but gauge is the quality signal — 22-gauge dents easily, resonates noise, poor mass. Plumber consensus: 'builder-grade filler' — most complaints about flexing, noise, and staining from standing water.
No calibration products. Reserved for brands with active safety recalls, non-cUPC-certified imports, or documented structural defects.

quality.notes: Fireclay (kiln-fired 2100°F+) and cast iron (porcelain enamel) are premium construction methods. 16-gauge T-304 stainless is professional-grade. 18-gauge is standard residential. 20+ gauge is builder-grade. Composite (80%+ granite/quartz + acrylic resin) is premium engineered material. Vitreous china is the bathroom standard. Lower gauge number = thicker steel = better.

Handcrafted (Rohl Shaws — each individually formed and kiln-fired) is the premium for fireclay. Zero-radius and tight-radius welded (precision CNC welding, true 90° or near-90° corners) is the premium for stainless — requires thicker steel. Drawn/pressed from a single sheet is standard. Mass-stamped is builder-grade — often results in thinner corners.

Kohler's porcelain enamel (cast iron) is industry benchmark — chip/stain/fade resistant. Blanco Silgranit (patented, 35+ patents) is the composite benchmark. Commercial satin finish on stainless hides scratches well. Standard vitreous china glaze is baseline for bathroom. Mirror polish shows every scratch.

Stainless-only spec. Cast iron, fireclay, and composite are inherently quiet (massive body absorbs vibration = N/A, +1 equivalent). Full pad + spray coating (Kraus NoiseDefend 80%+, Elkay Sound Guard) is premier. Partial pads = standard. No sound deadening = builder-grade, major complaint driver.

Apron-front/farmhouse requires specific cabinetry and professional installation — quality signal. Undermount is standard premium. Drop-in/self-rimming is the simplest, least premium installation. Flush-mount is aesthetic preference, neutral.

Rohl Shaws (+1, Darwen Lancashire England). Kohler (+1, Kohler WI USA for cast iron). Blanco (0, Germany HQ + global manufacturing). Kraus (0, identified factories). Elkay (+1, US manufacturing). Glacier Bay (-1, unknown OEM).

performance.notes: Sloped bottom with rear drain placement provides better drainage and usable basin space. Standard center drain is baseline. Flat bottom with poor slope causes pooling — common complaint on cheap sinks and some fireclay designs.
Kitchen only. Deep basin (10"+) provides capacity for large pots/sheet pans. Standard (8-9") is baseline. Shallow (<8") limits utility. Bathroom sinks are N/A (depth is adequate for purpose).

Kitchen only. Integrated ledge rails for cutting boards, colanders, drying racks are a genuine utility improvement. Kraus and Ruvati lead this space. Not having workstation features is NOT a penalty — it's a traditional design.

durability.notes: Cast iron enamel: 50+ years (Kohler lifetime). Fireclay: 50+ years with care. Composite: 25-50 years. Stainless 16-gauge: 25-50 years. Stainless 18-gauge: 15-25 years. Stainless 22+ gauge: under 15 years (flex fatigue, seal failure).

Stainless = excellent (doesn't chip, can dent). Composite = excellent (extremely hard, minor chips at extreme impact). Cast iron = good (enamel can chip, base survives). Fireclay = good (dense ceramic, but can crack at extreme impact — non-repairable). Thin-gauge stainless = poor (flex causes seal failure at mounting points).

All premium sink materials are inherently non-porous (stainless, fireclay glaze, cast iron enamel, composite). Susceptible = porous or degraded finishes that absorb stains. Key differentiator is how VISIBLE stains are — white fireclay shows tea/coffee marks more readily than composite or stainless.

Kitchen only. Cast iron enamel: extreme (withstands direct heat). Stainless: extreme (conducts but doesn't damage). Composite: good (Silgranit rated 536°F). Fireclay: extreme (kiln-fired at 2100°F). Acrylic/budget composite: limited.

Kohler: limited lifetime on cast iron. Rohl Shaws: limited lifetime. Blanco: limited lifetime on Silgranit. Kraus: limited lifetime. Elkay: limited lifetime on most. Glacier Bay: 1 year. Warranty term is a manufacturer confidence signal.

Sinks have simple parts ecosystems compared to appliances. Key parts: drain assembly, basket strainer, mounting hardware, sink grid/rack. Kohler/Elkay: universal aftermarket drain assemblies + brand grids. Blanco/Rohl: brand-specific accessories but widely available. Budget brands: generic parts.

scoring_rules: Kitchen sinks and bathroom sinks scored within the same framework. Sub-type (stainless, fireclay, cast iron, composite, vitreous china) does NOT create an automatic tier advantage — a premium stainless and a premium fireclay can both be Tier 1.

Stainless gauge is THE critical spec for stainless sinks. 16-gauge T-304 is professional-grade. 18-gauge is standard residential. 20+ gauge is builder-grade. Gauge is the strongest quality signal plumbers cite.
Construction method matters: handcrafted fireclay (individually formed) > zero-radius welded stainless (precision CNC) > drawn/pressed > stamped.

Sound deadening is a scored quality spec for stainless sinks. Full pad + spray coverage vs no coverage is a massive real-world difference. Cast iron, fireclay, and composite are inherently silent — this is a genuine material advantage, not a penalty on stainless.
Performance axis is essentially flat (like faucets). All sinks drain water. Depth, slope, and workstation integration create minor differentiation but the axis compresses. P=0.10.
Bathroom sinks are predominantly vitreous china. Differentiation comes from glazing quality, china density, rim engineering, and overflow mechanism — not from material class.
Kohler showroom vs Kohler retail may differ — score the specific product line, not the brand. Same rule as faucets (Rule 19).
Apron-front/farmhouse installation is a quality signal — requires custom cabinetry and professional installation. Drop-in is the simplest mounting, least premium.

Corporate structure = report finding (Kohler private family-owned since 1873, Rohl = Fortune Brands Innovations, Blanco = BLANC & FISCHER Family Holding, Kraus = private, Elkay = private family-owned since 1920).
Score base configuration. Note upgrade availability (e.g., workstation accessories, sink grids, custom drain finishes).
Warranty exclusion consistency rule applies. All sink warranties exclude abuse, misuse, and improper installation — don't penalize one brand for universal exclusions.
Fireclay sinks may have slight dimensional variations due to kiln-firing process — this is a feature of handcrafted manufacturing, not a defect.

material_safety_report_only: Lead content in glazes (not a concern in modern US production — lead-free standard)
Nickel leaching from stainless steel (negligible at T-304 grade, documented safe)
Antimicrobial agent type in coatings (silver-ion, copper-infused — FDA GRAS, no concern)
cUPC certification status (gate check — uncertified = excluded from scoring)
sub_type_note: Kitchen sinks (stainless, fireclay, cast iron, composite) and bathroom sinks (vitreous china, fireclay) are scored within the same framework. Sub-type-specific spec fields coexist — kitchen-only fields (sound_deadening, workstation_integration, basin_depth, heat_resistance) are omitted for bathroom products. Bathroom-only differentiation is captured through body_material, surface_finish_technology, and construction_method. Same approach as gas/induction in ranges_cooktops and tankless/tank/heat_pump in water_heaters.
